title: 40+ Tips I Wish I Knew Sooner | RuneScape: Dragonwilds
author: PHINQS
description:
I've spent 30+ hours playing RuneScape: Dragonwilds since its release, and during that time, I have developed a pretty strong understanding of the game.

So, I thought it would be a good idea to share this knowledge with the aim of helping other players get the best possible experience out of the game and avoid some of the same mistakes that I made.

These tips vary from beginner-friendly to more advanced and cover a wide range of areas in-game. For clarity, I have broken these tips down into the following seven categories:

- Food and drink
- Gathering
- Building
- Crafting
- Exploration
- General, and
- Combat

I have tried my best to avoid spoilers. However, given the nature of the video, it is possible that I will discuss parts of the game which you have not yet been exposed to.

ingredients into one recipe and make vegetable soup, you'd expect that I would receive at least 40 sustenance or
possibly even more since this is technically a higher tier food. But instead, if I eat this vegetable soup,
you'll see that in the bottom left of the screen, my sustenance only actually increases by 30. So, even though I used
the exact same ingredients, I actually lost a total of 10 sustenance from making vegetable soup rather than eating
these items individually. So, it seems that the only real advantage of higher quality foods is that they take less
time to consume overall and take up less space in your inventory. Another tip is that some foods also provide a status
effect in addition to providing sustenance. The earliest encounter of this is likely to be grilled mushrooms,
which can be made by cooking two butterc mushrooms found in the swamp. And this will provide you with an increased

order to fight or heal or, you know, drink a potion, whatever it may be. Another thing in combat, what you might
realize is that your armor, you seem to sort of make it and you put it on and you have a nice purple bar down in the
center of your screen down here. Now you can see here mine is currently saying 0 to 75. So I've obviously taken a little
bit of damage. And this is basically extra life that your armor can provide you on top of the resistance stats that
your armor is providing you. So in order to refill this back up, you need to come to your rune alter with some rune
essence and stone, I believe. Just go ahead and grab some of that. And then you can go ahead and make yourself some
ward stones. So let's make just one of them for now. And then once you come into your inventory and use one of these
up, you'll see uh I've now moved it up to 30 over 75. But something just bear in mind with
this is it does actually have some toxicity as well. So if you already have been drinking dirty water or something
else, this might sort of set you over the edge. So just be aware of that. This is something which comes with uh aspects
of a debuff whilst also delivering something quite positive too. So, now that we're on the topic of armor, let's
start speaking about set bonuses. So, you may have already seen when you're crafting your sets that you have these
set bonuses. So, it says here, if you have one piece of the three, you get stealth speed plus 40. If you have all
three, you get weak point damage plus the other two, for example. However, maybe you don't really have a good shot
and you know you you're not often hitting weak point damages when you're ranged because you like to aim for the
body and that's more of a sure shot for you, for example. Then maybe you don't need weak point damage. Maybe you just
want to be able to fire off more shots than you would need to if you were able to hit the weak point every time. So
then maybe the set bonus isn't so great for you to use. Maybe you would want to use something like hard leather body and
the chaps so that you can get the ranged attack stamina cost minus 33%. But then you've also got like a wizard hat for
example which is a minus 50% stamina regen delay. So having a stamina regen delay reduction and also stamina cost
reduction. you could probably shoot off quite a lot of arrows in a small period of time using a sort
of mixed set, mixed armor set like those three. And also, whilst we're just on the topic of this, I like to choose my
armor depending on what I feel like I'm likely to get hit by. So, when I'm in combat, if it's melee combat, then I
think that normally I can either block or parry any melee attacks. But something that I often get caught out by
is the range attacks from a ranger which quite far away that typically has very good accuracy and hits almost all the
time. So because of that, I've decided to opt for the ranged armor because it has a higher ranged defense. So this
means that I'm going to be taking less damage presumably from any ranged attacks. And this is something that I
find that I get hit from quite a lot and that's why I've opted for my armor. Obviously, that's going to be personal
preference, but that's the way it works in this game. It's not doesn't work exactly the way the OSRS works, and that
might help you progress through the game a little bit easier and make it a little bit easier for you. And last, but not
least, I just want to touch on the fact that some combat items, like this whip, have special attacks, and it's
definitely worth making use of them because they can have some powerful effects. This one for the whip, for
example, stuns opponents. Now I can just get in a few easy hits and sort of do a
lot of damage without really any risk to myself. If you made it this far in the video, you now know 40 tips which I wish

comments.author: @BrutalNap
comments.text:
I only played a few hours, but if i began all over again I would probably do the following 10 steps.

1. gather wood and stone, create a few campfires, fill them with wood and cook up like 400-500 water. This is to boost cooking past the early few levels. These can cook in the background while you do other things. This will let you speedrun to the range where you can combine food to make dishes and to the grill which doesn't require fuel like the campfire.
2 (SPOILER) There are usefull boots hidden on top of the windmill in the beginner area and a blueprint for a decent sword hidden on the cathedral roof. Get these.. Trust me. 
3. Cooked rat meat and cooked red berries give a fairly easy and decent starter meal when combined. Farm these and don't eat them individually.
4. Raw redberries and water makes a drink that slows down water consumption. Well worth it as i felt i was CONSTANTLY filling up my water bar.
5. Build wherever you want, but look for a fairly flat area to make things easier for yourself. Construction and Farming are two VERY important skills, so don't forget/neglect them. I also advices you to build near water/ponds to make life easier for yourself. 
6. GATHER FLAX WHENEVER YOU SEE IT... Trust me. You will need it! It's not rare, but it's not as easy to find as redberries or other wild vegetables. To go and actually scavenge for it can be a pain. Especially if you are sharing area together with others.
7. Remember chest locations. They will restock after a couple of days.
8. You'll first be introduced to melee, but try to keep magic and ranged level up around the same area.
9. Always carry rune essence to craft runes. Prioritize law runes as they are a must when teleporting with lodestones. One spawn is behind the cathedral you enter the world in.
10. I find myself constantly leveling up when i do everything within the world. Don't feel the need to powerlevel in the beginning. You can always go back to level up if you hit a skilling blockade. (If you are gonne power level something, then maybe start with agility. Unlocking doublejump and dash is so useful.
